# Ali Ahmed Awan

> Product leader and AI builder based in Lahore, Pakistan. Builds AI-driven products, leads product teams, and writes about product strategy, AI in production, growth, and leadership.

Ali Ahmed Awan has 10+ years leading products across Pakistan, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, West Africa, and the US. He leads Xcellerant Ventures' AI product portfolio (FastRead.io, Myautobio, Clintwin/Medsim AI, Formulai), founded Ovela Health (medical travel to Pakistan), and previously led product at The ENTERTAINER, PakWheels/ArabWheels, Tribal Health, Hexkode, and Vodlix. He also runs hands-on AI training workshops for business teams.

## Site

- [Home](https://aliahmedawan.me/): bio, services, case studies, AI training, contact
- [AI training](https://aliahmedawan.me/ai-training.html): hands-on workshops for business teams, from product squads to finance and accounting, including an AI for Managers and Leaders programme. Teams leave knowing where AI fits their work, what is safe to put into a public tool, how to prompt and check answers in Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, and how to turn one good result into a repeatable process. Duration, format, price and client names are not published on the site yet.
- [Blog](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/): 21 posts on product strategy, AI in production, growth, and leadership, since 2023

## Blog posts

### 2026

- [Benchmarking LLMs for production: what the leaderboards don't tell you](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/benchmarking-llms-for-production.html): Public leaderboards rank models on tasks that look nothing like yours. Here's how I actually evaluate Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini for production use.
- [What founding Ovela taught me that ten years of product management didn't](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/what-founding-taught-me.html): Product management teaches you how to make a decision well. Founding teaches you what it feels like when there's nobody above you to catch the ones you get wrong.

### 2025

- [How we cut AI running costs by 38% without making the output worse](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/cutting-ai-running-costs-38-percent.html): Benchmarking, routing and caching across four AI products. What actually moved the bill, and what didn't.
- [RAG isn't a model problem, it's a retrieval problem](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/rag-is-a-retrieval-problem.html): Swap the model all you want, if retrieval hands it the wrong paragraph confidently, no amount of model quality fixes what happens next.
- [Free trial or freemium? What doubling paid conversion taught me](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/free-trial-or-freemium.html): Lessons from moving a lifestyle app to freemium and subscriptions, and why onboarding mattered more than price.
- [Why concierge beats self-serve for high-stakes decisions](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/concierge-beats-self-serve.html): Self-serve won every growth argument I made for years, until I built a product where removing the human was the thing actively costing us trust.
- [Don't copy-paste your playbook into a new market](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/dont-copy-paste-your-playbook.html): What launching a car marketplace in the UAE and Saudi Arabia taught me about local buying behaviour.
- [Migrating off legacy software without breaking the business that runs on it](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/migrating-off-legacy-software.html): The real risk in a legacy migration was never the new platform failing. It was the four months in between, where both systems had to be true at once.
- [What managing a 17-person AI team taught me about letting go](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/managing-a-17-person-team.html): Scaling from a handful of engineers to a 17-person AI product team meant unlearning the habits that made me good at shipping, personally.

### 2024

- [Building a virtual patient: what medical simulation taught me about trust in AI](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/virtual-patients-and-trust-in-ai.html): Clintwin/Medsim AI isn't a chatbot with a medical skin on it. The entire design brief was about what happens when a model is convincing but wrong.
- [Agile stopped being about being agile](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/agile-stopped-being-about-being-agile.html): Most teams running 'agile' are running the ceremony with the actual agility quietly removed. Here's how to tell, and what to rebuild instead.
- [One number, one portfolio: picking a north star across four products](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/one-north-star-four-products.html): Four AI products, four different markets, one portfolio strategy. The hard part isn't picking a metric per product, it's resisting the urge to.
- [Your strategy is only as good as your execution](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/strategy-is-as-good-as-execution.html): The decision to go freemium took an afternoon. Making it work took a rebuilt product, forty interviews, and a year.
- [What I look for when hiring a PM who's never been one](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/hiring-a-first-time-pm.html): The best PM hire I ever made had never held the title. The signal I was actually looking for doesn't show up on a resume at all.
- [Stop scoring your roadmap. Start arguing about strategy.](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/strategy-over-scoring-models.html): Scoring frameworks don't resolve prioritization debates. They just launder someone's opinion through a formula that looks objective.

### 2023

- [Why 40 customer interviews beat one survey of 4,000 people](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/40-interviews-beat-one-survey.html): Surveys scale. Interviews don't. For the decisions that actually matter, that trade-off runs the wrong way more often than product teams admit.
- [Product-led growth only works if the product actually leads](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/product-led-growth-needs-a-product-that-leads.html): PLG became a label teams reach for before they've done the one thing it actually requires: letting the product sell itself.
- [What shipping an MVP in under 90 days actually requires you to cut](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/shipping-mvp-in-90-days.html): The hard part of a 90-day MVP was never the 90 days. It was agreeing, out loud, on what we were willing to be embarrassed about at launch.
- [Design thinking works better as a loop than a funnel](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/design-thinking-is-a-loop.html): The five stages of design thinking were never meant to run once, start to finish. Treating them that way is where most teams get stuck.
- [From business analyst to product manager: the move nobody tells you how to make](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/from-business-analyst-to-product-manager.html): Nobody hands you a product manager title. You just start doing the job, badly at first, until someone notices you already are one.
- [The CIRCLES method isn't just an interview trick](https://aliahmedawan.me/blog/circles-method-beyond-interviews.html): The interview-prep framework everyone memorizes and almost nobody uses on the job, until you actually try it.
